title: Post Correspondence Problem with three pairs is likely undecidable

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Post Correspondence Problem with three pairs is likely undecidable

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Whether a set of upper/lower block pairs can be concatenated to give identical strings (the Post Correspondence Problem) is straightforward for two pairs, but already with three pairs there is computational irreducibility, making the question undecidable in general.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: I strongly suspect that even with just three pairs there is already computational irreducibility

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 12, “The Principle of Computational Equivalence”; section “Undecidability and Intractability” (from p. 753), p. 756. Scope: Post Correspondence Problem instances with small numbers of pairs

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch12-22: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.86

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: This is a sharply defined decision-problem threshold that can be settled by published proof under explicit conventions. Public literature and proof checking are sufficient today, although the claim's wording conflates irreducibility with undecidability.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Formalize Post Correspondence Problem instances restricted to at most three pairs and establish either a decision algorithm or a reduction proving undecidability. A valid proof directly resolves the threshold claim, while enumeration can independently check bounded cases.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Computational irreducibility is not equivalent to undecidability.

The exact encoding restrictions on words and alphabets affect the threshold.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Existing proofs resolve the neighboring statements: two pairs are decidable, and five pairs suffice for undecidability. The sentence at issue is the three-pair case, which those proofs explicitly leave open. Machine-checked searches of bounded word lengths show that individual three-pair puzzles can be extremely hard, and a uniform decision procedure or an undecidability reduction is still required for the general claim.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: A decision procedure for every three-pair instance would refute undecidability; a reduction from the halting problem to three-pair Post correspondence would confirm it. Published proofs already settle the two-pair case as decidable and the five-pair case as undecidable, and they leave the three-pair threshold open.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The general three-pair problem is open; resolved finite instances leave the infinite family undecided.

Long minimal solutions show practical difficulty and are compatible with a yet-unknown decision procedure.
